alt: Compressing six huge values, two of them repeated, into small ranks: sorting the distinct values and numbering them from 0, then filling the compressed array one entry at a time by looking each original value up in the rank dictionary.

steps.caption: 6 values arrive, some repeated. Sorting the 4 distinct ones and numbering them from 0 gives rank = {7: 0, 42: 1, 500: 2, 999: 3}.
values[0] is 500; rank[500] is 2, so compressed[0] = 2.
values[1] is 7; rank[7] is 0, so compressed[1] = 0.
values[2] is 500; rank[500] is 2, so compressed[2] = 2.
values[3] is 42; rank[42] is 1, so compressed[3] = 1.
values[4] is 7; rank[7] is 0, so compressed[4] = 0.
values[5] is 999; rank[999] is 3, so compressed[5] = 3.
The compressed array only ever holds indices 0 through 3, however large the original values were.

values[3] is 321; rank[321] is 0, so compressed[3] = 0.

4 values arrive, some repeated. Sorting the 4 distinct ones and numbering them from 0 gives rank = {2: 0, 9: 1, 88: 2, 321: 3}.
values[0] is 9; rank[9] is 1, so compressed[0] = 1.
values[1] is 321; rank[321] is 3, so compressed[1] = 3.
values[2] is 2; rank[2] is 0, so compressed[2] = 0.
values[3] is 88; rank[88] is 2, so compressed[3] = 2.
